claude.rationale: The anchoring 2007 transaction was a sponsor-led acquisition in which CD&R/KKR acquired the pre-existing US Foodservice business whole from Royal Ahold, installing new controlling intent (T1=replace) while the operating vehicle, distribution product, network, and workforce transferred as a going concern. On gap_45, the customer-facing foodservice-distribution product (400,000+ SKUs to 250,000+ locations) is described as a single integrated product/operating network moving together with its 61 facilities, ~6,000 trucks and shared-services center, so product and its producing/delivering processes crossed the boundary jointly (0). On gap_56, the S-1 states the operating model was standardized and centralized after acquisition while management continuity was maintained (internal CEO promotion of Satriano; Lederer succession), indicating processes and the organization running them aligned coherently rather than diverging at closing (0).

gemini.rationale: The transaction described is an IPO/registration event where the existing sponsors (CD&R and KKR) maintain control and the entire operating company (US Foods) transfers as a whole. There is no evidence of structural mismatches between the product, processes, or organization at closing.

grok.rationale: The S-1 frames a single integrated customer-facing distribution product/operating network (400k+ SKUs, 61 facilities, shared-services center) assembled from the 2007 platform acquisition plus twelve further distributors, with concurrent standardization and centralization of business processes and a common technology infrastructure across those assembled businesses, so T4 and T5 crossed together with no product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0). Operating organization is documented as continuous via internal CEO promotion (Satriano from CMO) and Sponsor influence confined to a stockholders agreement and separate consulting agreements rather than direct operating management, so T5 and T6 were aligned at closing (gap_56=0).
